identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start (0,0). Moved down into a corridor; observed further down two cells, with a left branch at distance 2.
Start (0,0); moved down twice to (0,-2). Current corridor continues down; the next cell below has an opening left, so continue exploring downward before taking that branch.
Start (0,0); moved down three times to (0,-3). Down is blocked; current cell opens up and left. Explore the left branch now.
At (-1,-3) after moving left. Corridor continues left; the next cell left opens right and down. Continue left to explore the branch, then backtrack if needed.
At (-1,-3), continue left into the next corridor cell. It is expected to open down; inspect that branch next, then backtrack if it dead-ends.

At (-1,-3); left is blocked, so remain consistent with the known position and explore the open downward branch. If this dead-ends, backtrack right and investigate the corridor toward the upper branch.
At (-1,-2) after taking the downward branch. Down is now blocked; explore the open right corridor for three cells before backtracking. Up remains the route toward previously seen areas.
At (0,-2) after moving right from the side branch. The corridor continues right for two cells, while left returns toward explored territory. Continue right to inspect the unvisited corridor.
At (1,-2) after moving right. The corridor continues right to an unvisited junction with up and down branches; proceed right to explore it.
At (2,-2), right is blocked. This junction has unexplored up and down branches; take up first. The cell above opens right and down, so continue mapping upward before backtracking.
At (2,-1) after moving up from the junction. Up and left are blocked; inspect the open right dead-end cell first, then return to investigate the downward branch.
At (3,-1), the right branch was a dead end. Move left back to (2,-1), then investigate the unexplored downward branch.
Back at (2,-1) after checking the right dead end. The downward branch is unexplored; move down and map it before backtracking.
At (2,-2) after returning from the upper branch. The downward branch is unexplored; continue down into the visible cell, which opens up and left.
At (2,-3) after moving down; down is blocked. The left corridor is unexplored and extends three cells, so continue left to map it before backtracking.
At (0,-3). The left corridor is already mapped toward a dead end, while the right cell is the return route and has an upward branch visible beyond it. Backtrack right, then investigate upward.

At (1,-3). The left corridor leads through explored territory toward a dead end; move up into the previously mapped central corridor and continue systematic backtracking for any unvisited branch or exit.
At the junction after moving up. The upper branch has been checked, while the downward route leads into the partially explored lower corridor. Continue down to inspect any remaining branch or exit.
At (1,-3); the left corridor is explored and dead-ends. Move up to the junction, then backtrack left toward (-1,-2), whose upward branch remains unexplored.

At the central junction; upper, lower, and immediate left routes appear mapped. Backtrack left through the corridor toward the branch near (-1,-2), whose upward path remains the best unexplored route.
At (1,-2) after moving left from the central junction. Continue left through the corridor toward the previously unexplored upward branch near (-1,-2).
At (0,-2); move left into the corridor toward the branch near (-1,-2). Once there, investigate its upward route, which remains unexplored.
At (-1,-2), the unexplored upward branch is open. Take it to continue systematic exploration; the right corridor is already mapped.
At (-1,-1) after taking the previously unexplored upward branch. Up and left are blocked; the open right corridor extends two cells, while down returns to explored territory. Explore right.
At (0,-1) after moving right. The corridor continues right to a cell opening upward and left; continue right to inspect this remaining branch.
At (1,-1) after moving right. Right and down are blocked; the upward route is unexplored and continues through two visible cells, so move up to investigate it.
At (1,1) after moving up. The vertical corridor continues upward to a cell opening left, while down returns to explored territory. Continue upward to investigate the remaining branch.
At (1,2) after moving up. Up and right are blocked; the left branch is unexplored, while down leads through a known corridor. Explore left first.
At (0,2) after moving left from the upper branch. The right cell is known; take the open downward route to investigate the remaining corridor, backtracking if it is already explored.
At (0,1) after moving down from the upper branch. Down and right are blocked; up returns to the known upper corridor. The open left cell is the remaining unexplored direction, so investigate it.
At (-1,1) after moving left from the known upper corridor. Open routes are up and right; right returns to explored territory, so continue upward through the unexplored corridor.
At (-1,2) after moving up from (-1,1). The corridor continues upward for two cells, while down returns to explored territory. Continue upward to investigate the remaining unexplored path.
At (-1,3) after moving up. The cell above is a dead end, while the right corridor extends four cells and appears unexplored. Explore right systematically.
At (0,3) after moving right from the upper dead-end branch. The corridor continues right for three cells; proceed right to explore the unvisited route and inspect the upcoming junction.
At (1,3) after moving right. The corridor continues right for two cells toward an unexplored junction, while left returns to the mapped upper branch. Continue right to explore.
At (2,3) after moving right. The right cell is unexplored and opens down and left, while up is another unexplored branch. Explore right first, then backtrack to inspect up if needed.
At (3,3). Move right into the unexplored cell, which is visible as opening down and left. Inspect that branch before backtracking to the unexplored upward route.
At the junction reached after the blocked right move; right is blocked and the available unexplored branch is down. Move down to inspect it, keeping left as the return route.
At the lower branch junction, down is blocked. The right cell is open but appears to be a short dead end; inspect it first, then return left to investigate the remaining branch.
At (4,2) after moving right into a dead end. Only left is open; backtrack left to the junction at (3,2) and then investigate its remaining upward branch.
Back at the junction after checking the right dead end. The upward branch is the remaining unexplored route; take it and map the next area.

At the upper-right cell after exploring its upward branch. The right and up routes are blocked; down returns to the mapped lower junction. Move left toward the earlier junction at (2,3), whose upward branch remains unexplored.
At (2,3); left and right corridors are mapped, while the open upward branch is unexplored. Move up to investigate it.
At the unexplored upper branch after moving up. Up and left are blocked; right and down are open. Down returns to mapped territory, so explore right first and inspect the new corridor for the exit.
At the right dead end of the upper branch. Only left is open; backtrack left to the junction and then investigate the remaining downward route if needed.
Back at the upper junction after checking the right dead end. The downward route is the remaining unexplored direction from here; follow it to inspect the next junction and search for the exit.

At the junction after moving down. Down is blocked; right is a known dead-end route, while the left corridor leads toward the remaining mapped junctions and is the best route to continue systematic exploration for the exit.

At the horizontal corridor after moving left from the junction. Both directions are open, but the right side leads through already explored junctions; continue left to retrace and inspect the remaining corridor for an exit or unvisited branch.
At (0,2) after moving left. The corridor continues left to a junction with up, right, and down openings; move left to inspect this remaining branch and search for the exit.

At (-1,2) after moving left. Up is a dead end; the right corridor is long and provides the best route toward remaining junctions, while down returns through known territory. Continue right and watch for the exit.
At (0,2) after moving right from the left junction. The corridor extends three cells right and is the best remaining route to search for the exit; continue right through this corridor.
At (1,2) after moving right. The horizontal corridor continues right for two cells toward an unexplored junction; proceed right to continue searching for the exit.
At the junction after moving right. Up, right, and left are open; down is blocked. The right cell is the least recently explored and opens down and left, so continue right to inspect it.

At (3,3), matching the previously encountered upper-right cell. Left returns through explored corridor; down leads to the junction explored earlier and is the best remaining route to continue searching for the exit.
At (3,2), the right branch is open and leads to a one-cell dead end. Inspect it, then backtrack left to continue searching remaining corridors for the exit.
At the one-cell right dead end; only left is open. Backtrack left to the junction and continue systematic exploration through remaining corridors.
At (3,2) after backtracking from the right dead end. Right is exhausted; move left through the central corridor to revisit earlier junctions and search remaining routes for the exit.
At (2,2); right is explored and left/up are blocked. Take the open downward route through the lower corridor, revisiting its junctions to search for any missed exit.
At (2,1) after moving down from the central junction. Up returns to explored territory; the open right corridor appears to lead through a remaining branch. Explore right before backtracking.
At the horizontal corridor after moving right from (2,1). The right cell is unexplored and opens downward and left; continue right to inspect that branch for the exit.

At the newly reached corner after moving right. Up and right are blocked; down and left are open. Follow down first through the visible corridor, checking for an exit or any branch not previously explored.
At (4,0) after moving down from the corner. The corridor continues down, and the next cell opens left; continue downward to inspect that branch for the exit.
At (4,-1) after moving down. Down and right are blocked; up returns to the corridor, while left is the remaining branch and may lead toward the exit. Explore left.
At (3,-1) after moving left from the corridor corner. Right returns to the recently explored route; take the open downward branch to inspect the remaining path for the exit.
Exit is visible four cells to the right along the open corridor. Continue right toward it.
At (4,-2) after moving right. The exit remains visible three cells farther along the open right corridor; continue straight toward it.
At (5,-2) after moving right. The exit is visible two cells ahead along the open right corridor; continue right.
At (6,-2) after moving right. The exit is visible one cell ahead to the right; move right into it.
